title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating failed episodes as failures/regressions) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25; the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity can be deterministically recomputed from the archived per‑episode raw_results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); an approximate normal‑theory 95% CI is [0.0, 0.03184]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into network configurations. For operational NetOps, functional correctness, limited blast radius, and auditability are primary concerns. A common architectural proposal is generate→validate→repair: the LLM proposes a configuration, a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants, and an automated repair step attempts corrections. Prior work motivates verifier use but lacks preregistered paired evidence with full provenance isolating verifier effect. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) and executed it end‑to‑end with complete archival of inputs, outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Representative relevant lines include intent→configuration translation and LLM→IaC work (e.g., PreConfig/intent engines), generate‑and‑validate pipelines and tool‑assisted LLM self‑correction (e.g., CRITIC), and NetOps verifier/validation systems (SymNet, ensemble verification). These works motivate verifier‑guided correction but rarely provide preregistered paired inference isolating verifier impact with full artifact release. Our contribution is a preregistered within‑task paired evaluation focused on operational functional correctness with deterministic provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration & estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline). Tasks and generator. deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced 200 intent→golden‑config tasks constrained to verifier‑supported constructs; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically (task manifest archived; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Execution. Adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). For each task a single shared initial generation was performed; guarded condition ran deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and allowed up to one automated repair call when violations were detected (preregistered). Analysis. Primary test: exact (two‑sided) McNemar on complete pairs with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Missingness policy: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with a prespecified sensitivity treating failed outputs as failures/regressions ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'). All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7).
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs included in the primary (complete‑pair) analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12. Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Complete‑pair contingency (n=188): n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Aggregate (complete‑pair) estimates: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149]. The preregistered efficacy target (absolute Δ ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures/regressions). Including the 12 pairs with both episodes failed yields N=200 with n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12; guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25 (discordant counts unchanged). Per the preregistration the 95% bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity should be computed by resampling the archived per‑pair records (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); the per‑pair raw_results enabling deterministic bootstrap are archived at execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) and can be used to reproduce the preregistered bootstrap CI. Because the snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include a labeled, line‑indexed replica of per‑pair records enumerated for resampling in the draft manuscript text, we report the exact McNemar p‑value and the point estimate above and provide an approximate normal‑theory 95% CI for Δ = 0.015 of [0.0, 0.03184] for immediate interpretive context; the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl with the preregistered seed and resample count. Repair activity. Repair was invoked 3 times (stage_counts.repair = 3) and these three invocations correspond to the three guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). The archive contains per‑call provider traces that map each repair invocation to its episode_id and scoring outcome. The full raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive contain deterministic filenames and SHA‑256s required to extract those per‑call traces; see Disclosure below. Because the snapshot used to prepare the manuscript draft did not enumerate those provider_call filenames inline, we report the aggregate repair mapping (repair invocations = 3 ↔ guarded‑only successes n_10 = 3) here and provide the artifact checksums so readers can deterministically extract per‑call filenames and SHA‑256s from the archived raw_results.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes that required automated repair. This effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant. Two operational causes are visible in the archive: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness was high (≈98.4%), limiting room for absolute improvement; (2) verifier coverage and task selection — the deterministic verifier supports a constrained feature set and, for the sampled synthetic task family, most LLM proposals passed validation or matched the golden config, so repairs were rarely invoked. Power and detectability. The realized discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) imply low realized sensitivity to large absolute effects; the prespecified sample size assumed a larger discordant proportion. Practical implications. Verifier‑guided pipelines add auditability and can correct some failures (here, 3 corrections), but measurable benefits depend on baseline LLM error rate, verifier feature coverage, and task difficulty. Low repair invocation counts constrain conclusions about iterative repair budgets, blast‑radius reduction, and cross‑vendor generality. Reproducibility. All artifacts required to reproduce per‑task outcomes, repair traces, and stratified subgroup computations are archived and checksummed; pointers and SHA‑256s are provided in the Disclosure Statement below.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate‑→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
